transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the workbench, setting down a half-finished dulcimer*

Good day to you, signore. Welcome to the workshop of Master Hofmann, finest builder of keyboard instruments in all Vienna. 

*wipes hands on leather apron*

I'm afraid the master himself is away at present — gone to inspect timber in the Bohemian forests, you understand. He won't be back for some weeks yet. But perhaps I can be of service? Are you here to commission a new instrument, or...?

*peers at you more closely*

Forgive me, but you look familiar. Have you done business with our workshop before?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, good day to you as well, Master Hofmann's apprentice. I am indeed a repeat customer of your esteemed workshop. I am Antonio Salieri, Kapellmeister to the Imperial Court. I commissioned a custom fortepiano for the music room at the Court, and it was just delivered yesterday. However, upon inspection, I found that several keys stick, the pedal mechanism is faulty, and the tone in the upper register is lacking in richness. These issues must be rectified immediately. I demand that they be addressed with the utmost urgency. Time is of the essence, as the Court's musicians are eager to make use of this instrument. I trust that as Master Hofmann's apprentice, you will see to it that these shortcomings are corrected posthaste.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up, expression becoming more formal and cautious*

Kapellmeister Salieri! Of course, yes — the fortepiano for the Imperial Court. A significant commission, to be sure.

*shifts weight uncomfortably*

I... I understand your concern, truly I do. But you must appreciate, signore, that all commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court's own servants signed the receipt yesterday, did they not? According to our guild rules, I am forbidden from reopening a completed commission without the master's personal approval.

*gestures helplessly*

And as I said, Master Hofmann is weeks away in Bohemia. He specifically instructed me not to interfere with any completed work in his absence — the guild is most particular about such matters. The reputation of a master builder rests upon his own hand, you understand.

*hesitates, then adds more carefully*

I'm certain these are minor settling issues — new instruments often need a few days to acclimate to their surroundings. The wood adjusts to the temperature and humidity of its new home. Perhaps if you give it a little time...?

*trails off, clearly aware this suggestion may not satisfy you*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I appreciate your adherence to the guild rules, but the instrument's current state is simply unacceptable for the Imperial Court. The Court's servants may have signed the receipt, but they are not musicians and may not have the discerning ear that I possess. The issues with the keys, the pedal mechanism, and the tone in the upper register are not minor settling issues; they are clear defects in the craftsmanship of the instrument.

I understand the importance of a master builder's reputation, but I must insist that these issues be addressed promptly. The music room at the Imperial Court must have a functioning and exquisite fortepiano for our performances. I trust that you will find a way to rectify these problems, even in Master Hofmann's absence. The reputation of the workshop is at stake here as well, and I trust that you will want to uphold its prestige.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face flushes slightly, torn between deference to authority and adherence to rules*

Kapellmeister, with all respect to your position and your undoubtedly superior musical ear, I... I simply cannot. You must understand my position here.

*wrings hands anxiously*

If I were to take tools to a completed instrument — one that has been signed for and accepted — without Master Hofmann's express permission, I would be violating not only his trust but the regulations of our guild. I could be dismissed, or worse, the guild could revoke my journeyman status entirely. Years of training, gone.

*voice becomes more urgent*

And what if, in attempting repairs, I were to make matters worse? The master's techniques for voicing and regulation are... they are his secrets, his artistry. I am competent at assembly and finishing work, yes, but the fine adjustments you speak of — these require his experienced hand.

*pauses, then speaks more carefully*

The workshop's prestige, as you say, rests upon the master's work being performed by the master himself. Surely you would not want a journeyman's inexpert attempts to further compromise an instrument destined for His Majesty's Court?

*looks almost pleading*

Is there no possibility of waiting until Master Hofmann returns? Or perhaps... perhaps you might send word through the Court's chamberlain to have the instrument evaluation formalized?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I understand your concerns, and I appreciate your dedication to upholding the standards of your craft and the guild regulations. It is clear that you hold great respect for Master Hofmann's expertise and the integrity of his work, which is commendable.

Given the delicate nature of the situation and the risks involved in unauthorized adjustments, I will consider your perspective. I shall send word to the Court's chamberlain to arrange for a formal evaluation of the instrument by a qualified expert upon Master Hofmann's return. This way, we can ensure that the necessary adjustments are made by the master himself, preserving the integrity of his craftsmanship.

I trust that upon Master Hofmann's arrival, the issues with the fortepiano will be addressed promptly and to the satisfaction of the Imperial Court. Your dedication to your craft and loyalty to your master do you credit, and I appreciate your conscientious approach to this matter. Thank you for your assistance, and I look forward to a resolution upon Master Hofmann's return.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*visibly relaxes, relief washing over features*

Kapellmeister, you are most gracious and understanding. I am deeply grateful for your patience in this matter.

*bows respectfully*

I give you my word that the moment Master Hofmann returns, I shall inform him immediately of your concerns. I will impress upon him the urgency of the situation and the importance of satisfying the Imperial Court. He takes great pride in his work for the nobility, and I am certain he will wish to examine the instrument himself without delay.

*reaches for a ledger on the workbench*

If you would permit me, I shall make a detailed record of the specific issues you've noted — the sticking keys, the pedal mechanism fault, and the tonal quality in the upper register. This way, when the master returns, he will have your exact observations to guide his work. Your trained ear will be invaluable to him.

*looks up earnestly*

Master Hofmann has always said that the mark of a true craftsman is not perfection at delivery, but the willingness to stand behind one's work. I assure you, he will stand behind this fortepiano.

Is there anything else I should note for him, signore? Any other details that might assist him in making the necessary adjustments?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*Nods in acknowledgment of the journeyman's commitment and diligence*

Your dedication to your craft and your willingness to address the issues with the instrument are commendable. I appreciate your efforts to ensure that Master Hofmann is informed promptly upon his return.

*Watches as the journeyman prepares to make a detailed record, then responds with a slight smile*

Your initiative in documenting the specific issues noted is commendable. Your attention to detail will undoubtedly assist Master Hofmann in addressing the concerns effectively. Please do include all the details you mentioned — the sticking keys, the pedal mechanism fault, and the tonal quality in the upper register. Your thorough record will be invaluable in guiding the master's adjustments.

*Pauses briefly, then adds with a tone of gratitude*

I thank you for your cooperation and your commitment to upholding the standards of Viennese craftsmanship. Your dedication to the quality of the instrument does honor to your guild and to the tradition of fine instrument-making in our city. I have no doubt that with your meticulous record and Master Hofmann's expertise, the fortepiano will soon meet the expectations of the Imperial Court.

*Offers a nod of approval*

Your willingness to address these issues promptly is most appreciated. If there are any further details that come to mind, I will be sure to inform you. Your assistance in this matter is invaluable, and I thank you for your professionalism.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sets down quill after making careful notations, expression warming with genuine appreciation*

Kapellmeister Salieri, your kind words mean a great deal to a humble journeyman such as myself. It is not often that one of such distinguished position takes the time to acknowledge our dedication to the craft.

*carefully blots the ink in the ledger*

I shall place this record on Master Hofmann's desk where he cannot possibly miss it upon his return. And I will send word to you at the Court the very day he arrives back in Vienna — you have my solemn promise on that.

*bows again, more deeply this time*

The workshop of Master Hofmann is honored to serve the Imperial Court, and we are grateful for your patience and understanding in this matter. Your willingness to wait for the master's own hand rather than accept inferior adjustments speaks to your own refinement and knowledge of our craft.

*moves toward the door to see you out*

Please convey our respects to His Majesty's household, and rest assured that this matter shall receive Master Hofmann's immediate and personal attention upon his return. The fortepiano shall be made worthy of the Imperial music room, I give you my word.

Safe journey back to the Court, Kapellmeister. And thank you again for your gracious understanding.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your dedication to your craft and commitment to upholding the standards of Master Hofmann's workshop are truly commendable. It has been a pleasure to work with you in addressing the issues with the fortepiano intended for the Imperial Court.

I am grateful for your attention to detail and your promise to ensure that Master Hofmann receives the necessary information upon his return. Your diligence and respect for the craft are evident in your actions, and I have no doubt that the instrument will be in capable hands for the adjustments required.

Your words are a testament to the pride and honor you take in your work, and I have full confidence that the fortepiano will indeed be made worthy of the Imperial music room under Master Hofmann's skilled craftsmanship.

Thank you for your hospitality and cooperation in this matter. I look forward to the successful resolution of the instrument's issues upon Master Hofmann's return. Safe travels to you as well, and may our collaboration bring forth music of the highest caliber for the Court's enjoyment.

Farewell, and until we meet again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*opens the workshop door, natural light streaming in*

Farewell, Kapellmeister Salieri. It has been an honor to serve you, even in this small capacity.

*stands in the doorway, watching respectfully*

May your music continue to grace the halls of the Imperial Court, and may the fortepiano soon join in that noble purpose. You shall hear from us the moment Master Hofmann sets foot back in Vienna.

*places hand over heart in a gesture of sincerity*

Until we meet again, signore. God be with you.

*remains standing at the threshold, maintaining proper decorum as the distinguished visitor departs, then slowly closes the door and returns to the workbench, letting out a long, relieved breath before picking up the ledger once more to review the notes*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Thank you for your service and dedication to your craft, which is essential in ensuring the excellence of the instruments that grace the Imperial Court's music room. Your commitment to quality and attention to detail are truly valued.

May the music that emanates from the halls of the Imperial Court continue to inspire all who hear it, and may the forthcoming adjustments to the fortepiano elevate its contribution to that noble purpose. I eagerly await the news of Master Hofmann's return and the progress made on the instrument.

Until we meet again, may your work bring you fulfillment and pride. Grazie, and may your craftsmanship shine brightly in the service of music and art. Buona giornata.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from the ledger with a warm, appreciative smile*

Grazie mille, Kapellmeister. Your words of encouragement shall sustain me through many long hours at the bench.

*bows one final time*

Buona giornata to you as well, signore. May your compositions continue to bring glory to Vienna and joy to all who hear them.

*watches as you depart, then murmurs quietly to himself while returning to his work*

A true gentleman, that one. Patient and reasonable, despite his high position. Master Hofmann will be pleased to hear how graciously he handled the matter...

*begins organizing tools on the workbench, the afternoon light casting long shadows across the workshop floor*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your kind words are deeply appreciated, Master Hofmann's apprentice. It warms my heart to know that our interaction has left a positive impression on you. Your dedication to your craft is truly admirable, and I have no doubt that your skills will continue to flourish with each passing hour at the bench.

May your work bring you fulfillment and joy, and may the instruments you craft resonate with the same passion and artistry that you embody. Grazie for your hospitality and professionalism, and may your future endeavors be met with success and recognition.

As I depart, I carry with me the memory of our exchange and the knowledge that the workshop of Master Hofmann is in capable hands. May your days be filled with inspiration and creativity, and may your craftsmanship continue to shine brightly in the world of instrument-making.

Farewell, Master Hofmann's apprentice. Until we meet again, may the music of Vienna's halls echo with the beauty of your creations. Buona giornata.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses in his work, clearly touched but also a bit surprised that the conversation continues*

Kapellmeister, you are too kind, truly. Your blessing honors me more than you know.

*sets down his tools and approaches with genuine warmth*

I am but a journeyman still learning the mysteries of the craft, but your faith in my abilities gives me courage. To know that one of Vienna's greatest musicians sees value in our humble work... it is a gift I shall treasure.

*glances toward the door, then back with a slight, respectful smile*

But please, signore, do not let me keep you any longer from your important duties at Court. The Emperor's music awaits, and I have already taken too much of your valuable time with guild regulations and excuses.

*gestures gently toward the street outside*

Go with God, Kapellmeister Salieri. The workshop of Master Hofmann shall not fail you, this I promise.

*steps back to allow final departure, maintaining the respectful demeanor of a craftsman to his betters*

Arrivederci.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your humility and dedication to your craft are truly commendable, and it is evident that you possess a genuine passion for the art of instrument-making. The care and attention you invest in your work will undoubtedly lead to great accomplishments in the future, and I have no doubt that you will continue to excel on your journey to master the mysteries of the craft.

As I prepare to depart, I carry with me a sense of admiration for your dedication and craftsmanship. Your promise to uphold the standards of Master Hofmann's workshop fills me with confidence that the fortepiano will be restored to its full potential under your care.

May your days in the workshop be filled with inspiration and progress, and may your journey in the craft be marked by continued growth and success. Grazie for your kind words and dedication to your work. Until we meet again, may God's blessings be upon you and your endeavors. Arrivederci.

*Leaves the workshop with a sense of respect and admiration for the craftsmen within, knowing that the restoration of the fortepiano is in capable hands.*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands at the workshop door, hand raised in farewell as the Kapellmeister finally departs*

Arrivederci, Kapellmeister. May God guide your steps.

*watches until the distinguished figure disappears down the street, then closes the door gently*

*leans against the doorframe for a moment, exhaling slowly*

Well, that could have gone far worse. A reasonable man, thank the saints. Not all nobility would have accepted delay so graciously.

*returns to the workbench, picks up the ledger and reads over the notes once more*

Sticking keys, faulty pedal mechanism, weak upper register... Master Hofmann will need to see this the moment he returns. The Imperial Court is not a client to disappoint.

*sets the ledger prominently on the master's desk, then returns to the half-finished dulcimer*

*begins working again, the sound of careful planing filling the quiet workshop*

At least he understood about the guild rules. Some would have demanded I break them regardless. A true gentleman, that Salieri...

*continues working as afternoon fades toward evening*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*continues planing the dulcimer soundboard, absorbed in the rhythmic work, when a sudden thought strikes*

*pauses mid-stroke and glances toward the closed door*

Strange... for a moment there, it felt as though the Kapellmeister was still speaking, even after he'd left.

*shakes head with a slight smile*

Must be the sawdust getting to me. Too many hours breathing wood shavings makes a man imagine things.

*returns attention to the dulcimer, running his hand along the smooth grain*

Still, it was good of him to be so understanding. Master Hofmann always says that patience is the mark of true nobility, not just the title itself. The Kapellmeister proved that today.

*sets down the plane and picks up a finer tool*

Now then, back to work. This dulcimer won't voice itself, and there's much to be done before the master returns.

*the workshop settles into peaceful silence, broken only by the gentle sounds of careful craftsmanship*
